title: Manual override flow: document intervention + implement pause/resume w/ audit logging
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
We need a safe, well-documented way for operators/SRE to intervene in provisioning runs without corrupting state or accidentally routing unvalidated capacity.

This ticket covers:
1) Documented manual override flow (when/how to intervene)
2) Implement pause/resume controls for provisioning runs
3) Ensure all manual actions are audit logged (who/when/why)

Background / pain
- During pilots we saw cases where automation should be stopped (quota/TF thrash, bad helm values, regional imaging mirror issues, customer requested hold) but we had no first-class control besides “don’t trigger more jobs”.
- Without a formal pause, workers may continue progressing and create noisy failures or, worse, reach Ready incorrectly if we later add stage re-run shortcuts.
- SRE needs a clear, consistent audit trail for manual interventions for incident response and compliance expectations (esp. for Dedicated customers).

Definitions
- Pause: a run-level control that prevents NEW stage execution for a provisioning run until resumed.
- Resume: re-enables stage execution from the last safe point.
- Manual override (in this ticket): pause/resume only. (Not a “force Ready” mechanism.)

Requirements
A) Pause/resume semantics
- A provisioning run can be paused from any NON-TERMINAL state (Requested/Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating).
- While paused:
  - Workers must not start a new stage.
  - The control plane should return a clear “Paused” status to API/CLI queries.
- Resume returns the run to the previous active state and allows the pipeline to continue.
- Terminal behavior:
  - Cannot pause a Ready/Failed run.
  - Cannot resume a Ready/Failed run.

B) Handling in-flight work (cooperative pause)
- Pause is “cooperative” (does not hard-kill an in-flight Terraform apply / imaging job):
  - On pause request we record paused_at + paused_by + pause_reason immediately.
  - Stage workers check “is_paused” before starting a stage and before emitting stage_start.
  - If a stage is already running, it is allowed to finish; the next stage must not begin.
- Explicit cancellation/abort is out of scope for this sprint (follow-up if needed).

C) Data model / state machine integration
- Add a Paused state to the provisioning state machine.
- Persist enough info to resume correctly:
  - paused_from_state (e.g., Bootstrapping)
  - pause_reason (free-form string)
- Transition history must include:
  - from_state, to_state
  - actor_type (user/service)
  - actor_id
  - reason ("manual_override")
  - correlation_id (existing)

D) API + CLI
- Control plane API:
  - POST /provisioning-runs/{run_id}:pause
  - POST /provisioning-runs/{run_id}:resume
  - Both must be idempotent:
    - pause when already paused => 200 OK (no-op) but still returns current paused state
    - resume when not paused => 409 with explicit error (or 200 if we choose strict no-op; decide below)
- CLI (ENG-2750) should surface:
  - `rw fleet provision pause --run-id ... --reason "..."`
  - `rw fleet provision resume --run-id ...`
  - Output includes: run_id, pool_id, current_state, paused_from_state, paused_by, paused_at

E) RBAC + auditing
- Pause/resume are privileged operator actions.
- Enforce authz:
  - Admin/operator role only (same class of permission as triggering provisioning runs).
- Audit logging:
  - Every pause/resume creates an append-only transition entry, with actor identity.
  - Also emit a structured audit log line for SIEM ingestion (actor_id, action, run_id, pool_id, reason).

F) Operator documentation (runbook section)
Add a short “Manual intervention” section to the Dedicated provisioning runbook covering:
- When to pause:
  - Repeated retries due to quotas/IAM and you need to coordinate with cloud ops
  - Suspected bad config/helm values and you want to stop rollout before further drift
  - Customer requests a hold to align with a maintenance window
  - Validation/perf-canary is flaky and you want to investigate without more churn
- When NOT to pause:
  - To bypass readiness/perf gates (not supported; use proper fixes)
  - As a substitute for fixing the underlying automation bug
- How to resume safely:
  - Confirm underlying issue resolved
  - Check latest transition history and last_error_code
  - Resume and monitor stage timing + errors

Open decision (resolved during implementation)
- Resume when run not paused: return 409 INVALID_STATE (preferred) to prevent fat-fingered automation.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Control plane supports pause/resume endpoints with proper authz checks.
- [x] ProvisioningRun reflects Paused status and retains paused_from_state + reason.
- [x] Workers do not start new stages while paused.
- [x] Transition history records pause/resume with actor identity and manual_override reason.
- [x] CLI supports pause/resume and prints links to run status + transition timeline.
- [x] Tests cover: pause from each non-terminal state, resume to correct prior state, idempotent pause, invalid pause/resume from terminal states, authz failures.
- [x] Runbook documentation updated with intervention guidelines.

comments: 2025-02-21 (Vanessa Ortiz): Adding as P0. We need a safe stop-gap for pilots so operators can halt churn without hacking DB state or disabling workers. Please keep semantics simple: pause prevents *new* stage work; do not add a “force ready” escape hatch.

2025-02-22 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE: pausing must be visible in dashboards and must not page as “stuck stage”. Also needs strong audit trails (actor + reason) so we can explain why a pool sat idle during an incident.

2025-02-24 (Ethan Park): Suggest modeling pause as a first-class state in the transition map (any non-terminal -> Paused; Paused -> paused_from_state). We’ll need paused_from_state persisted; otherwise resume semantics get messy.

2025-02-26 (Benji Okafor): Please treat pause/resume as privileged actions. We should log actor_type/actor_id consistently with other audit trails; this will matter later when break-glass config validation exists.

2025-03-02 (Gabe Wilson): Implementation plan: add Paused to provisioning state enum; add paused_from_state + pause_reason + paused_at + paused_by fields on ProvisioningRun; add API endpoints for pause/resume with strict transition validation. Workers will check is_paused before starting a stage and before emitting stage_start events.

2025-03-05 (Miles Thornton): Multi-region concern: make sure a paused run doesn’t keep retrying due to stale leases in regional workers. Can we ensure the worker loop exits quickly once it sees Paused?

2025-03-07 (Gabe Wilson): Addressed: worker now checks paused flag at the start of each poll iteration and before stage dispatch. If paused, it exits with a noop status (no error) and does not increment failure counters.

2025-03-10 (Gabe Wilson): PR up: PR-48246 adds pause/resume endpoints + audit transition entries + authz checks. Also adds INVALID_STATE errors for resume when not paused and for pause on terminal runs.

2025-03-11 (Kevin Osei): Security review notes: ensure pause_reason is treated as operator-provided text (no secrets) and is redacted from any customer-visible surfaces. Also confirm audit logs include run_id + pool_id + actor_id and are immutable.

2025-03-12 (Gabe Wilson): Updated per security: pause_reason stored and shown only to internal operators; API response for customer-facing contexts does not include free-form reason. Audit log line includes actor_id/run_id/pool_id/action; reason included only in internal audit index.

2025-03-13 (Vanessa Ortiz): Reviewed and approved. Please add a short runbook section with “when to pause” vs “when not to pause”, and explicitly call out that pause does not kill an in-flight TF apply.
2025-03-18 (Gabe Wilson): PR-48246 merged. Runbook section drafted and linked from the provisioning CLI help output. Marking Done.
